overview: The profile uses Asteroxylon mackiei as a specimen-level exemplar of early lycopsid rooting architecture and does not project that anatomy onto every lycophyte.

ecology.habitat: Terrestrial; wetland to diverse modern habitats across the clade
ecology.bodySize: Small herbaceous forms to extinct tree-sized lycopsids
ecology.guild: Primary producer; no single clade-wide ecological guild

traits: Asteroxylon root-bearing and rooting axes as a species-level exemplar
evidenceSummary: Three-dimensional Rhynie-chert reconstruction directly supports Asteroxylon anatomy; it is not a direct ancestor, universal lycophyte body plan or proof of the clade’s 425 Ma endpoint.

overview: Metzgeriothallus sharonae provides a Middle Devonian liverwort body-fossil anchor, while Ordovician spore evidence remains a qualified affinity rather than a crown assignment.

ecology.habitat: Terrestrial moist-substrate association inferred for the fossil and common in living forms
ecology.bodySize: Small thalloid gametophyte in the profiled fossil

traits: Medial costa and bifurcation in Metzgeriothallus
Associated sporophyte capsule in the fossil sample
evidenceSummary: Givetian specimens support a liverwort body-fossil record and anatomy; older cryptospore and sporangial evidence does not securely set crown-Marchantiophyta first appearance.

overview: Aglaophyton major is represented here by Edwards's re-examination of new and historical Rhynie-chert material, which established the genus and reconstructed its axes and conducting strand without assigning it to a living higher group.

ecology.diet: Photosynthetic land-plant identity; carbon acquisition was not measured in the fossils
ecology.habitat: Rhynie Chert depositional context; the cited redescription does not establish a genus-wide habitat
ecology.locomotion: Sessile growth reconstructed from decumbent and upright axes
ecology.bodySize: Short plant reconstructed from sampled axes; no genus-wide population range
ecology.guild: Primary producer by plant identity; no detailed ecological guild is assigned

traits: Decumbent axes forming stands in the reconstruction
Dichotomously branching upright axes with terminal sporangia
Three-zoned conducting strand without differential wall thickenings
evidenceSummary: The 1986 redescription directly supports the named genus, sampled anatomy and reconstruction. The separate Rhynie U-Pb study supplies only a locality-age window, not a global genus duration, direct ancestor or settled higher placement.

overview: Horneophyton lignieri is represented by a 24-section museum sample, with three historical thin sections selected for confocal imaging that revised the interpretation of its conducting tissues without making the fossil a direct ancestor.

ecology.diet: Photosynthetic land-plant identity; carbon acquisition was not measured in the fossils
ecology.habitat: Rhynie Chert sinter-surface association reported in the study context; ecological breadth is unresolved
ecology.locomotion: Sessile growth; locomotor performance does not apply
ecology.bodySize: Diminutive reconstructed plant; the sampled thin sections do not define a population range
ecology.guild: Primary producer by plant identity; transport function remains inferred from preserved cells

traits: Rhizoid-bearing rhizome and bifurcating aerial axes in the reconstruction
Papillate wall ingrowths in conducting cells
No distinct xylem and phloem recovered by the confocal analysis
evidenceSummary: Confocal microscopy and three-dimensional modelling directly document cell-wall form in named NHMUK slides. Transfer-cell resemblance and transport function remain interpretations, while the independent locality-age window is not a global range or origin date.
